title: Amazon Science introduces controllable text-to-speech for audiobooks
excerpt: The system uses natural-language captions to improve character voice consistency and dialogue differentiation in long-form audio.
bodyHtml:
Amazon Science announced on October 23, 2026, a controllable text-to-speech (TTS) system designed to enhance audiobook narration. The technology allows for the control of speech delivery through natural-language captions, such as "whispering nervously" or "shouting in anger," enabling the model to synthesize speech with specific emotional or stylistic characteristics.

The system utilizes a component called BookLLM to identify unique characters and assign them consistent voice profiles throughout an entire book. According to Amazon Science, the system achieved 97% accuracy in identifying dialogue in English and 94% in Spanish. This process involves building a cast list and ranking characters by importance to derive voice descriptions.

Testing showed that rendering distinct character voices improved dialogue differentiation by 3.7 points on a MUSHRA listener-rating scale. The researchers observed statistically significant improvement in the listening experience for eight out of ten voices across both English and Spanish tests.
